        ↓
Baseline Chemical Knowledge Corpus


NEXT PHASE

Phase 9 — Geometry-Aware Molecular Encoder


---
==================================
PHASE 9 — GEOMETRY-AWARE EQUIVARIANT MOLECULAR ENCODER


OBJECTIVE

Phase 9 constructs the geometry-aware molecular encoder that transforms each
Phase 7 molecular graph into a continuous latent molecular representation.

The input molecular graph is:

G = (V, E, X, R)

where:

V = molecular atoms

E = bidirectional chemical-bond connectivity

X = invariant atomic feature matrix

R = centered three-dimensional Cartesian coordinates


The encoder transforms:

G
↓
Geometry-aware atom representations
↓
Equivariant message passing
↓
Molecular-level representation
↓
μ and log σ²
↓
Latent representation z


The resulting latent variable belongs to the continuous molecular latent space:

z ∈ Z


==================================================
PRIMARY INPUT
==================================================

Phase 8 provides the fixed baseline graph corpus:

Total graph corpus:

767 molecular graphs


Primary subsets:

Training corpus   = 613 graphs

Validation corpus = 76 graphs

Test corpus       = 78 graphs

Fisher reference  = 128 graphs


The Fisher reference corpus remains reserved for later Fisher-information
estimation and EWC.

It should NOT be treated as a separate training or validation dataset.


==================================================
GRAPH INPUT
==================================================

Each Phase 7 graph contains:

graph_id

drug_id

drug_name

standardized_smiles

x

edge_index

edge_attr

pos


where:

x = node feature matrix X

edge_index = graph connectivity E

edge_attr = chemical bond attributes

pos = centered Cartesian coordinates R


From Phase 7:

node feature dimension = 21

edge feature dimension = 14


These values should be read from the Phase 7 metadata/schema rather than
silently hard-coded wherever possible.


==================================================
PHASE 9 DATA FLOW
==================================================

Phase 8 Training Graphs
        ↓
Load Phase 7 .pt Graph Files
        ↓
Node / Edge Feature Preparation
        ↓
Initial Atom Embedding
        ↓
Geometry-Aware Equivariant Message Passing
        ↓
Layer 1
        ↓
Layer 2
        ↓
Updated Atomic Hidden Representations
        ↓
Permutation-Invariant Molecular Pooling
        ↓
Molecular Embedding h_G
        ↓
Latent Parameter Heads
        ├── μ
        └── log σ²
        ↓
Reparameterization
        ↓
z = μ + σ ⊙ ε
        ↓
Continuous Molecular Latent Representation


==================================================
1. IMPORTANT ARCHITECTURAL DISTINCTION
==================================================

The molecular encoder should distinguish between:

INVARIANT FEATURES

and:

GEOMETRIC COORDINATES


Atomic attributes X are scalar/invariant chemical features.

Examples:

atomic number
degree
formal charge
hybridization
aromaticity
chirality
hydrogen information
ring membership


Coordinates R contain geometric information:

x-coordinate
y-coordinate
z-coordinate


Absolute Cartesian coordinates must NOT simply be concatenated into ordinary
scalar node features.


The coordinate matrix must enter the model through the geometry-aware
message-passing mechanism.


==================================================
2. INITIAL ATOM EMBEDDING
==================================================

The original Phase 7 node feature vector has dimension:

21


Map each node feature vector into the encoder hidden space:

X_i
↓
Linear / MLP projection
↓
h_i^(0)


Recommended initial hidden dimension:

HIDDEN_DIM = 64


Therefore:

h_i^(0) ∈ R^64


The initial feature projection may conceptually be:

Linear(21 → 64)
↓
SiLU
↓
Layer Normalization


The exact architecture should remain lightweight because the current
baseline corpus contains only 613 training molecules.


==================================================
3. EDGE REPRESENTATION
==================================================

Phase 7 provides:

edge_attr dimension = 14


These attributes describe chemical bonds and include information such as:

bond type
conjugation
ring membership
stereochemistry


Edge attributes should contribute to the message function.


For an edge:

i → j


the message can depend on:

h_i
h_j
edge_attr_ij
distance_ij


where:

distance_ij = ||r_i - r_j||


==================================================
4. GEOMETRIC RELATIONSHIPS
==================================================

For connected atoms i and j:

r_ij = r_i - r_j


and:

d_ij² = ||r_i - r_j||²


Relative distances are invariant to:

global translation

global rotation


Relative coordinate vectors transform consistently under spatial
transformations and can therefore support equivariant coordinate updates.


The architecture should NOT rely on absolute molecular orientation.


==================================================
5. EGNN-STYLE MESSAGE FUNCTION
==================================================

A lightweight EGNN-style interaction can be expressed conceptually as:

m_ij = φ_e(
    h_i,
    h_j,
    d_ij²,
    e_ij
)


where:

m_ij = message from atom j to atom i

h_i, h_j = node representations

d_ij² = squared interatomic distance

e_ij = bond/edge attributes

φ_e = learnable edge-message network


This allows the encoder to combine:

chemical topology

atomic properties

bond information

three-dimensional geometry


==================================================
6. COORDINATE-AWARE / EQUIVARIANT UPDATE
==================================================

To retain the intended equivariant component, coordinate information should
participate through relative coordinates.

An EGNN-style coordinate update can conceptually be written as:

r_i^(l+1)
=
r_i^(l)
+
Σ_j
(r_i^(l) - r_j^(l))
φ_x(m_ij)


where:

φ_x

produces a learned scalar coefficient.


Because the coordinate update is based on relative coordinate vectors and
learned scalar functions, the geometric state transforms consistently under
global translations and rotations.


IMPORTANT:

If coordinates are used only to calculate fixed distances and coordinates are
never updated or otherwise handled equivariantly, the architecture should be
described conservatively as:

geometry-aware / distance-aware

rather than making a stronger equivariance claim.


Therefore the implementation should explicitly preserve the equivariant
coordinate-update mechanism if the patent architecture requires it.


==================================================
7. NODE FEATURE UPDATE
==================================================

Aggregate messages arriving at atom i:

m_i = Σ_j m_ij


Then update the node representation:

h_i^(l+1)
=
φ_h(
    h_i^(l),
    m_i
)


Possible implementation:

message aggregation
↓
MLP
↓
residual connection
↓
normalization


Residual updates are recommended for training stability.


==================================================
8. NUMBER OF MESSAGE-PASSING LAYERS
==================================================

For the baseline implementation use:

2 EGNN-style message-passing layers


Conceptually:

Initial Atom Embeddings
        ↓
EGNN Layer 1
        ↓
EGNN Layer 2
        ↓
Final Atomic Representations


This preserves the lightweight architecture from the original patent
implementation while incorporating explicit three-dimensional geometry.


==================================================
9. GRAPH / MOLECULAR POOLING
==================================================

Molecules contain different numbers of atoms.

Therefore the final node representations must be converted into one
fixed-dimensional molecular representation.


Recommended baseline:

mean pooling


For molecule G:

h_G
=
(1 / |V|)
Σ_i h_i


Mean pooling is:

permutation invariant

independent of molecular atom ordering

compatible with variable graph sizes


Optional later experiments may compare:

sum pooling
attention pooling
set-based pooling


But mean pooling is sufficient for the baseline implementation.


==================================================
10. IMPORTANT INVARIANCE PROPERTY
==================================================

The internal geometric processing may be equivariant.

However, the final molecular representation should be invariant to arbitrary
global molecular orientation and translation.


Therefore:

h_G

μ

log σ²

z


should not change materially simply because the entire molecule is:

rotated

or

translated


This is an important property that should be tested computationally.


==================================================
11. LATENT PARAMETERIZATION
==================================================

From pooled molecular embedding h_G, construct two output heads:

μ = f_μ(h_G)

log σ² = f_logvar(h_G)


Recommended latent dimension from the project configuration:

LATENT_DIM = 32


Therefore:

μ ∈ R^32

log σ² ∈ R^32


==================================================
12. WHY μ AND log σ² ARE USED
==================================================

The encoder is designed as a variational molecular encoder.

Instead of mapping each molecule directly to one deterministic point, the
encoder represents the molecule as a latent probability distribution:

q(z|G)
=
N(
    μ,
    diag(σ²)
)


This provides a continuous latent molecular representation that can later be
used by the molecular decoder and candidate-generation mechanism.


==================================================
13. REPARAMETERIZATION TRICK
==================================================

During stochastic latent sampling:

σ = exp(0.5 × log σ²)


Sample:

ε ~ N(0, I)


Then:

z = μ + σ ⊙ ε


This is the reparameterization trick.


It allows gradients to propagate through the latent sampling operation during
later end-to-end training.


==================================================
14. TRAINING AND EVALUATION LATENT POLICY
==================================================

A clear policy should be used.


During stochastic training:

z = μ + σ ⊙ ε


For deterministic validation / testing / representation extraction:

z = μ


Using μ for deterministic evaluation avoids random differences between
repeated evaluations of the same molecule.


==================================================
15. LATENT DIMENSION
==================================================

Use:

LATENT_DIM = 32


This matches the project configuration established earlier.


Therefore each molecule obtains a compact representation:

z ∈ R^32


==================================================
16. FEATURE NORMALIZATION
==================================================

Some Phase 7 node attributes are continuous numerical features.

Examples may include:

atomic mass
degree
formal charge
valence-related values


If numerical standardization is applied, the normalization statistics must be
computed using:

TRAINING DATA ONLY


Do NOT calculate normalization means or standard deviations using:

validation data

test data


This prevents preprocessing leakage.


The fitted normalization parameters should then be frozen and reused for:

training
validation
test
Fisher-reference graphs


Categorical one-hot features should not be standardized as if they were
continuous measurements.


==================================================
17. MINI-BATCH GRAPH PROCESSING
==================================================

Molecules contain different numbers of atoms.

The encoder therefore requires graph batching.


A batch should retain:

concatenated node features

concatenated coordinates

adjusted edge indices

edge attributes

graph-membership / batch vector


The batch vector indicates which molecule each atom belongs to.


Conceptually:

batch = [
    graph 0 nodes,
    graph 1 nodes,
    graph 2 nodes,
    ...
]


Global pooling should use this membership vector to generate:

one molecular embedding per graph.


==================================================
18. TRAINING DATA POLICY
==================================================

Only:

D_train

should be used to fit model parameters.


D_validation

should be used for:

model-selection diagnostics
early-stopping diagnostics
hyperparameter evaluation


D_test

must remain untouched during model development and should be used only for
final held-out evaluation.


D_fisher_reference

must remain reserved for later Fisher-information estimation.


==================================================
19. IMPORTANT PHASE BOUNDARY
==================================================

Phase 9 should define and validate the encoder architecture.


However, μ, log σ² and z do NOT automatically constitute a scientifically
meaningful learned latent molecular manifold merely because the forward pass
can compute them.


A learning objective is required.


If the molecular decoder and reconstruction objective are introduced in the
next phase, the baseline variational encoder should be trained jointly with
that objective rather than claiming that an untrained Phase 9 encoder has
already learned chemical representations.


Therefore Phase 9 should clearly distinguish:

MODEL CONSTRUCTION

from:

MODEL LEARNING


==================================================
20. RECOMMENDED PHASE-9 BASELINE SCOPE
==================================================

Phase 9 should perform:

graph dataset loading

mini-batch construction

training-only feature normalization preparation

initial node embedding construction

edge-aware geometry-aware message passing

two EGNN-style layers

equivariant coordinate handling

global molecular pooling

μ projection

log σ² projection

reparameterization function

latent dimensionality validation

forward-pass validation

rotation/translation consistency testing

gradient-flow sanity testing

model parameter-count reporting


Phase 9 should establish that the encoder is computationally correct.


==================================================
21. PHASE 9 SHOULD NOT YET PERFORM
==================================================

Full encoder-decoder optimization

molecular reconstruction training

SMILES decoding

SELFIES decoding

candidate molecule generation

QED optimization

SA optimization

biological relevance prediction

UCB acquisition

Fisher-information estimation

EWC regularization

closed-loop molecular adaptation


These belong to later phases.


==================================================
22. FORWARD OUTPUT
==================================================

For every molecular graph batch, the encoder should return at minimum:

mu

logvar

z


Recommended optional outputs for diagnostics:

graph_embedding

final_node_embeddings

updated_coordinates


Conceptually:

encoder(G)
→ {
    μ,
    log σ²,
    z
}


==================================================
23. LATENT OUTPUT
==================================



---
=====================
PHASE 10 — BASELINE VARIATIONAL LATENT REPRESENTATION LEARNING


OBJECTIVE

Phase 10 trains the previously initialized geometry-aware variational molecular
encoder so that DrugBank molecular graphs are mapped into a structured,
continuous latent molecular representation space.

Phase 9 constructed and computationally validated the encoder architecture.

Phase 10 performs the first actual representation-learning stage.


The encoder maps:

G = (V, E, X, R)

to:

μ(G)

and:

log σ²(G)


which define the approximate latent distribution:

q(z|G)

=
N(
    μ(G),
    diag(σ²(G))
)


A latent representation is sampled using:

z
=
μ
+
σ ⊙ ε


where:

σ
=
exp(
    0.5 × log σ²
)


and:

ε ~ N(0, I)


The latent vector has dimensionality:

z ∈ R^32


==================================================
IMPORTANT CONCEPTUAL DISTINCTION
==================================================

The complete scientific progression is:

DrugBank XML
        ↓
Chemical Knowledge Source
        ↓
Standardized Molecular Representation
        ↓
Geometry-Aware Molecular Graph
        ↓
G = (V,E,X,R)
        ↓
Geometry-Aware Equivariant Encoder
        ↓
μ and log σ²
        ↓
Variational Learning
        ↓
z ∈ R^32
        ↓
Learned Baseline Molecular Representation


Therefore:

XML
=
chemical knowledge source


Graph representation
=
computational molecular representation


Latent space
=
learned molecular representation


These three concepts should remain clearly separated throughout the
implementation and research documentation.


==================================================
PRIMARY INPUT
==================================================

Phase 8 provides the fixed molecular subsets:

Training corpus:

613 graphs


Validation corpus:

76 graphs


Test corpus:

78 graphs


Fisher reference corpus:

128 training-derived graphs


Phase 9 provides:

geometry-aware equivariant variational encoder

NODE_FEATURE_DIM = 21

EDGE_FEATURE_DIM = 14

HIDDEN_DIM = 64

LATENT_DIM = 32

NUM_EGNN_LAYERS = 2


and:

training-only feature normalization parameters.


==================================================
IMPORTANT DATA POLICY
==================================================

Only:

D_train

may be used to update model parameters.


D_validation

may be used for:

validation loss

early stopping

model selection

training diagnostics


D_test

must NOT influence:

gradient updates

early stopping

hyperparameter selection

checkpoint selection


The test corpus should remain untouched until the final baseline model has been
selected.


D_fisher_reference

must also remain untouched during ordinary baseline representation learning.


It is reserved for later:

Fisher-information estimation

and:

Elastic Weight Consolidation.


==================================================
WHY PHASE 10 IS NECESSARY
==================================================

Phase 9 produced an initialized encoder capable of computing:

μ

log σ²

z


However, the model parameters were random/untrained.


Therefore the Phase 9 latent outputs do NOT yet represent a learned molecular
manifold.


Phase 10 introduces a learning objective that updates the encoder parameters so
that the latent representation contains information about molecular structure.


==================================================
1. VARIATIONAL LATENT DISTRIBUTION
==================================================

For each molecular graph G, the encoder produces:

μ(G)

and:

log σ²(G)


These define:

qφ(z|G)

=
N(
    μ(G),
    diag(σ²(G))
)


where:

φ

denotes the encoder parameters.


During training:

z
=
μ
+
σ ⊙ ε


where:

ε ~ N(0,I)


During deterministic evaluation:

z = μ


This ensures reproducible molecular embeddings for:

validation

testing

visualization

similarity analysis

later Fisher estimation.


==================================================
2. A LEARNING SIGNAL IS REQUIRED
==================================================

A variational encoder cannot learn useful molecular representations from the
KL-divergence term alone.


The model requires a reconstruction or predictive objective that forces z to
retain information about the input molecule.


Therefore Phase 10 should introduce a baseline molecular reconstruction
mechanism.


Conceptually:

Molecular Graph G
        ↓
Encoder
        ↓
μ, log σ²
        ↓
z
        ↓
Decoder / Reconstruction Heads
        ↓
Predicted Molecular Information
        ↓
Reconstruction Loss


==================================================
3. BASELINE DECODER STRATEGY
==================================================

For the first baseline implementation, the decoder does NOT need to generate a
complete chemically valid molecule yet.


Instead, lightweight reconstruction heads can be used to reconstruct meaningful
graph-level molecular descriptors or pooled structural representations.


This keeps Phase 10 focused on:

learning the baseline latent representation


rather than immediately solving the much harder problem of full molecular
generation.


Possible reconstruction targets include selected molecular-level properties
derived directly from the input graph.


Examples:

number of atoms

number of heavy atoms

number of bonds

mean node-feature representation

aggregated bond-feature representation

selected normalized structural descriptors


The exact reconstruction targets must be derived only from the existing graph
representation and should not introduce information from the validation or test
sets.


==================================================
4. WHY NOT FULL SMILES GENERATION YET
==================================================

Full molecular generation requires additional design decisions involving:

sequence decoder architecture

SMILES or SELFIES vocabulary

tokenization

sequence padding

teacher forcing

validity constraints

chemical reconstruction evaluation


Introducing all of these simultaneously with the first latent-learning stage
would make it difficult to determine whether problems originate from:

the encoder

the latent representation

or the sequence decoder.


Therefore the recommended progression is:

Phase 10
=
baseline latent representation learning


Later phase
=
full molecular decoder / candidate generation


==================================================
5. RECONSTRUCTION TARGET VECTOR
==================================================

For each molecular graph G, construct a deterministic graph-level target vector:

y_G


The target should summarize structural information already contained in the
molecular graph.


One recommended baseline is:

y_G
=
[
    mean node features,
    mean edge features,
    normalized graph-size descriptors
]


For example:

mean(X)

mean(edge_attr)

normalized number of nodes

normalized number of bonds

normalized number of heavy atoms


Because Phase 7 provides:

21 node features

14 edge features


the reconstruction target could contain approximately:

21 node-summary dimensions

+

14 edge-summary dimensions

+

3 graph-size dimensions


giving:

38 reconstruction dimensions


The exact dimension should be explicitly documented by the implementation.


==================================================
6. TRAINING-ONLY TARGET NORMALIZATION
==================================================

Any continuous graph-level reconstruction target must be normalized using
statistics derived from:

TRAINING DATA ONLY


The resulting mean and standard deviation values are then frozen and reused for:

training

validation

test


This prevents information leakage.


==================================================
7. LATENT DECODER / RECONSTRUCTION HEAD
==================================================

A lightweight decoder can map:

z ∈ R^32

to:

ŷ_G


Conceptually:

z
↓
Linear
↓
SiLU
↓
Linear
↓
Reconstructed graph-level target


Recommended baseline:

32
→
64
→
reconstruction dimension


This decoder is intentionally lightweight.


Its purpose is to provide a learning signal for the latent representation.


It should NOT yet be described as a molecular generator.


==================================================
8. RECONSTRUCTION LOSS
==================================================

For continuous reconstruction targets, a simple baseline objective is:

L_recon
=
MSE(
    ŷ_G,
    y_G
)


where:

ŷ_G

is the decoder prediction


and:

y_G

is the true molecular reconstruction target.


This encourages z to preserve structural information about the molecular graph.


==================================================
9. KL-DIVERGENCE REGULARIZATION
==================================================

The variational latent representation should also be regularized toward a
standard Gaussian prior:

p(z)
=
N(0,I)


The KL divergence for each molecule is:

L_KL
=
-1/2
Σ
[
    1
    +
    log σ²
    -
    μ²
    -
    exp(log σ²)
]


This prevents the latent space from becoming an arbitrary collection of
disconnected deterministic codes.


It encourages:

continuity

smoothness

sampling compatibility

latent-space regularity.


==================================================
10. TOTAL VARIATIONAL OBJECTIVE
==================================================

The baseline Phase 10 loss should combine:

reconstruction loss

and:

KL-divergence loss


Conceptually:

L_total
=
L_recon
+
β L_KL


where:

β

controls the strength of latent regularization.


For the initial experiment, a relatively small KL weight is recommended so
that reconstruction learning is not overwhelmed early in training.


For example:

BETA_KL = 0.001


This is a baseline hyperparameter and must be documented rather than treated as
a universally optimal value.


==================================================
11. KL ANNEALING
==================================================

A useful improvement is to gradually introduce KL regularization during the
first part of training.


Conceptually:

β_t
=
β_max × annealing_factor


Early epochs:

β_t ≈ 0


Later epochs:

β_t → β_max


This reduces the risk of:

posterior collapse


where the encoder ignores the molecular input and produces latent
distributions that are too close to the prior.


For the first implementation, either:

fixed small β

or:

simple linear KL warm-up


is acceptable.


If KL annealing is implemented, it must be recorded in the experiment
configuration.


==================================================
12. TRAINING PROCEDURE
==================================================

For every training batch:

1. Load molecular graphs.

2. Apply Phase 9 training-derived feature normalization.

3. Pass graphs through the geometry-aware encoder.

4. Obtain:

   μ

   log σ²

   z

5. Construct or retrieve reconstruction targets.

6. Decode z into predicted reconstruction targets.

7. Calculate reconstruction loss.

8. Calculate KL divergence.

9. Calculate total loss.

10. Backpropagate gradients.

11. Update encoder and reconstruction-decoder parameters.


Conceptually:

G
↓
Encoder
↓
μ, log σ²
↓
z
↓
Reconstruction Decoder
↓
ŷ
↓
Reconstruction Loss

+

KL Loss

↓
Total Loss

↓
Backpropagation


==================================================
13. OPTIMIZER
==================================================

A suitable baseline optimizer is:

Adam


Recommended starting learning rate:

LEARNING_RATE = 1e-3


The learning rate should be recorded in the model configuration.


No claim should be made that this is the optimal hyperparameter without
systematic comparison.


==================================================
14. TRAINING EPOCHS
==================================================

The implementation should define a maximum number of epochs.


For example:

MAX_EPOCHS = 100


However, the final model should preferably be selected using validation
performance rather than simply taking the final epoch.


==================================================
15. EARLY STOPPING
==================================================

Use the validation corpus for early stopping.


Monitor:

validation total loss


or preferably both:

validation reconstruction loss

validation KL loss


A reasonable baseline patience may be:

10–15 epochs


The checkpoint with the best validation objective should be retained.


The test dataset must not participate in early stopping.


==================================================
16. MODEL CHECKPOINTING
==================================================

Save at minimum:

best encoder state

best reconstruction-decoder state

optimizer-independent model configuration

normalization metadata

best epoch

training loss

validation loss


Recommended files:

phase10_best_encoder.pt

phase10_best_latent_decoder.pt

phase10_training_history.csv

phase10_training_config.json

phase10_training_summary.json


==================================================
17. BASELINE LATENT REPRESENTATION EXTRACTION
==================================================

After selecting the best model, switch to deterministic encoding:

z = μ


Generate latent vectors for:

training corpus

validation corpus

test corpus


Each latent vector should have dimension:

32


Recommended outputs:

phase10_train_latent.csv

phase10_validation_latent.csv

phase10_test_latent.csv


Each row should contain:

graph_id

drug_id

drug_name

z_0

z_1

...

z_31


For clarity, these deterministic latent vectors may also be referred to as:

μ-based baseline molecular embeddings.


==================================================
18. FISHER REFERENCE POLICY
==================================================

The Fisher-reference corpus was selected from the training corpus in Phase 8.


During Phase 10:

do NOT calculate Fisher information yet.


However, once the best baseline encoder has been selected, deterministic
baseline embeddings for Fisher-reference molecules may optionally be saved for
diagnostic purposes.


The actual Fisher-information calculation belongs to a later continual-learning
phase.


==================================================
19. LATENT SPACE QUALITY CHECKS
==================================================

After training, Phase 10 should examine whether the latent representation is
numerically and structurally usable.


At minimum evaluate:

finite latent values

latent mean

latent standard deviation

per-dimension variance

duplicate latent vectors

near-zero-variance dimensions

extremely large latent values


The representation should not collapse to a single identical vector for all
molecules.


==================================================
20. POSTERIOR-COLLAPSE CHECK
==================================================

Posterior collapse is an important risk in variational learning.


Possible warning signs include:

μ approximately zero for every molecule

log σ² approximately zero for every molecule

very small latent variance across the dataset

KL divergence approaching zero immediately

decoder reconstruction remaining poor


Therefore Phase 10 should explicitly monitor:

mean KL loss

latent variance

reconstruction loss


Posterior collapse should be reported rather than silently ignored.


==================================================
21. RECONSTRUCTION PERFORMANCE
==================================================

Report reconstruction error separately for:

training corpus

validation corpus

test corpus


Do not report only the total variational loss.


Recommended metrics include:

MSE

MAE


These provide interpretable evidence that the learned latent vector retains
information about molecular structure.


==================================================
22. LATENT SIMILARITY ANALYSIS
==================================================

The learned latent space may later support molecular similarity analysis.


For deterministic embeddings:

z = μ


possible comparisons include:

Euclidean distance

cosine similarity


However, Phase 10 should initially treat these as descriptive latent-space
diagnostics.


Do NOT immediately claim that nearby molecules are pharmacologically equivalent.


==================================================
23. STRUCTURAL RELATIONSHIP CLAIMS
==================================================

The Phase 10 objective is based primarily on chemical graph reconstruction.


Therefore the strongest justified initial interpretation is:

structurally related molecular representations may organize into meaningful
regions of latent space.


A stronger claim such as:

"pharmacologically related molecules cluster together"


requires explicit biological supervision or separate quantitative validation.


DrugBank target associations alone should not automatically be interpreted as
measured binding-affinity supervision.


==================================================
24. OPTIONAL BIOLOGICAL VALIDATION
==================================================

Phase 6 biological associations may later be used to evaluate whether molecules
sharing:

targets

actions

or human biological associations


show measurable latent-space organization.


This should be treated as:

post-training biological validation


rather than the core Phase 10 reconstruction objective.


Biological information should remain separate from the chemical encoder input
unless an explicitly supervised multimodal model is later introduced.


==================================================
25. IMPORTANT TEST-SET POLICY
==================================================

The test corpus should be evaluated only after:

training is complete

the best validation checkpoint is selected


The test result represents held-out baseline generalization.


Do NOT repeatedly inspect test performance while adjusting model
hyperparameters.


==================================================
26. MODEL STATUS AFTER PHASE 10
==================================================

Unlike Phase 9, the encoder will now have undergone parameter optimization.


Therefore after successful Phase 10 training it is appropriate to describe the
model as:

TRAINED BASELINE GEOMETRY-AWARE VARIATIONAL ENCODER


It is then reasonable to state that:

the model has learned a baseline continuous molecular representation from the
DrugBank-derived molecular graph corpus.


However, avoid overstating what the latent space represents.


It is primarily a learned:

chemical / structural molecular representation


unless additional biological validation demonstrates stronger properties.


==================================================
27. WHAT PHASE 10 SHOULD PERFORM
==================================================

Phase 10 should perform:

loading the initialized Phase 9 encoder

loading training/validation/test molecular graphs

reusing Phase 9 normalization

constructing molecular reconstruction targets

training-only reconstruction-target normalization

constructing a lightweight latent reconstruction decoder

variational sampling

reconstruction-loss calculation

KL-divergence calculation

total-loss calculation

encoder optimization

decoder optimization

validation monitoring

early stopping

best-checkpoint selection

deterministic latent extraction

latent quality-control analysis

reconstruction evaluation

training-history recording


==================================================
28. WHAT PHASE 10 SHOULD NOT PERFORM

Phase 10 should NOT yet perform:

full molecular generation

SMILES generation

SELFIES generation

novel candidate generation

QED-based optimization

SA-based optimization

target bioactivity prediction

UCB acquisition

Fisher-information estimation

EWC regularization

closed-loop adaptation


These belong to later phases.

==================================================
31. COMPLETION CRITERIA
==================================================

Phase 10 is complete when:

1. Phase 9 initialized encoder is loaded successfully.

2. Phase 8 training corpus is used for optimization.

3. Validation corpus is used only for validation/model selection.

4. Test corpus is excluded from parameter optimization.

5. Fisher reference corpus remains excluded from Fisher calculation.

6. Phase 9 normalization parameters are reused.

7. Reconstruction targets are defined deterministically.

8. Reconstruction-target normalization is fitted on training data only.

9. Latent reconstruction decoder is implemented.

10. μ is produced for each molecular graph.

11. log σ² is produced for each molecular graph.

12. stochastic reparameterization is used during training.

13. reconstruction loss is calculated.

14. KL-divergence loss is calculated.

15. total variational loss is calculated.

16. gradients update encoder parameters.

17. gradients update latent-decoder parameters.

18. validation loss is monitored.

19. early stopping / best-checkpoint selection is implemented.

20. best model checkpoint is saved.

21. best model checkpoint can be reloaded.

22. deterministic latent extraction uses z = μ.

23. 32-dimensional latent vectors are produced.

24. train latent vectors are saved.

25. validation latent vectors are saved.

26. test latent vectors are saved.

27. all latent vectors contain finite values.

28. latent variance is evaluated.

29. posterior collapse is checked.

30. reconstruction metrics are reported separately.

31. Phase-8 split assignments remain unchanged.

32. no Fisher information is calculated.

33. no EWC is applied.

34. no candidate molecules are generated.

35. the trained baseline latent molecular representation is ready for later
    decoder/generative and continual-learning stages.


==================================================
IMPORTANT TERMINOLOGY AFTER PHASE 10
==================================================

After successful Phase 10 training, it is appropriate to say:

"The geometry-aware variational encoder was trained on the DrugBank-derived
baseline molecular graph corpus to learn a continuous structural molecular
representation."


It is also appropriate to say:

"A baseline latent molecular representation was established."


Do NOT yet claim:

"The model learned binding affinity."

"The model predicts therapeutic efficacy."

"The model discovered pharmacologically superior molecules."

"The latent space is biologically optimal."


Those claims would require additional evidence and later experimental stages.

==================================================

        ↓

        ↓

        ↓

        ↓

        ↓
Lightweight Reconstruction Decoder
        ↓
Predicted Structural Summary
        ↓
Reconstruction Loss
        +

        ↓
Variational Training Objective
        ↓
Backpropagation
        ↓
Updated Encoder + Decoder
        ↓
Validation / Early Stopping
        ↓
Best Baseline Model
        ↓
Deterministic Encoding
        ↓
z = μ
        ↓
Baseline Learned Molecular Latent Representation

Phase 11 — Molecular Decoder / Generative Representation Development

---

PHASE 11 — MOLECULAR DECODER AND CANDIDATE GENERATION MODULE


OBJECTIVE

Phase 11 extends the trained baseline molecular latent representation from
Phase 10 into a generative molecular system.

The trained geometry-aware encoder maps molecular graphs into:

z ∈ R^32


Phase 11 introduces a generative decoder that learns the reverse relationship:

Latent representation
        ↓
Sequence decoder
        ↓
Molecular sequence
        ↓
SELFIES
        ↓
Decoded molecular structure
        ↓
Canonical SMILES
        ↓
Chemical quality-control filtering
        ↓
Valid candidate molecules


The purpose of Phase 11 is to establish a computationally manageable
latent-to-molecule generation mechanism.

It is NOT yet the closed-loop optimization stage.


==================================================
IMPORTANT PHASE-10 → PHASE-11 DISTINCTION
==================================================

Phase 10 trained:

Graph
↓
Geometry-aware encoder
↓
z
↓
Structural-summary reconstruction


The Phase-10 lightweight decoder was NOT a molecular generator.


Therefore Phase 11 introduces a separate:

GENERATIVE SEQUENCE DECODER


The new decoder must learn:

z
→
molecular sequence


It should not reuse the Phase-10 structural reconstruction head as though it
could directly generate molecules.


==================================================
PRIMARY INPUT
==================================================

Phase 10 provides:

trained geometry-aware variational encoder

best encoder checkpoint

32-dimensional deterministic molecular embeddings

training latent vectors

validation latent vectors

test latent vectors


Phase 5 provides:

standardized molecular structures


The sequence-generation target should be based on:

standardized_smiles


or a derived:

SELFIES representation


The molecular structures used for decoder training must correspond to the same
DrugBank molecule IDs used in the Phase-8 split.


==================================================
DATA POLICY
==================================================

Training molecules:

613


Validation molecules:

76


Test molecules:

78


The same Phase-8 molecule-level split must be preserved.


Only training molecules may update decoder parameters.


Validation molecules may be used for:

decoder validation

early stopping

model selection


Test molecules must remain excluded from:

parameter optimization

early stopping

hyperparameter selection


The Fisher-reference subset remains unrelated to decoder training and should
remain reserved for later continual-learning stages.


==================================================
1. GENERATIVE REPRESENTATION
==================================================

Recommended primary representation:

SELFIES


Conceptually:

standardized SMILES
        ↓
SELFIES conversion
        ↓
SELFIES token sequence


SELFIES is recommended because it reduces the frequency of syntactically
invalid molecular strings during generation.


However:

SELFIES validity does NOT remove the need for chemical validation.


Every generated molecule must still be checked using a chemistry toolkit such
as RDKit.


==================================================
2. WHY SELFIES IS PREFERRED FOR THE BASELINE
==================================================

Direct SMILES generation can fail because generated sequences may contain:

unclosed rings

invalid branches

invalid atom syntax

incorrect token combinations


SELFIES provides a more robust molecular sequence representation.


Therefore the preferred pipeline is:

z
↓
SELFIES decoder
↓
Generated SELFIES
↓
SELFIES-to-SMILES conversion
↓
RDKit molecular parsing
↓
Chemical QC


SMILES should still be stored because it is useful for:

RDKit processing

canonicalization

comparison

downstream evaluation.


==================================================
3. TOKENIZATION
==================================================

Construct the decoder vocabulary using:

TRAINING MOLECULES ONLY


Required special tokens:

<PAD>

<BOS>

<EOS>

<UNK>


where:

PAD = sequence padding

BOS = beginning of sequence

EOS = end of sequence

UNK = unknown token


SELFIES tokens should remain chemically meaningful units rather than
character-level splitting.


Example conceptual sequence:

<BOS>
[C]
[C]
[O]
<EOS>


==================================================
4. VOCABULARY LEAKAGE POLICY
==================================================

The decoder vocabulary should be built from:

training molecular sequences only.


Validation and test sequences must not be used to construct the vocabulary.


If a validation/test molecule contains an unseen token:

<UNK>

or another explicitly documented handling mechanism should be used.


This prevents sequence-vocabulary leakage.


==================================================
5. SEQUENCE LENGTH
==================================================

Determine sequence lengths using training data.


A maximum decoder length must be defined.


The selected value should be based on the observed training sequence
distribution rather than an arbitrary extremely large value.


Report:

minimum sequence length

median sequence length

maximum sequence length

selected decoder maximum length

number of molecules truncated


Prefer a maximum length that avoids truncating training molecules where
computationally feasible.


==================================================
6. GENERATIVE DECODER ARCHITECTURE
==================================================

A very large transformer is not necessary for the baseline implementation.


Recommended lightweight architecture:

Latent vector z
        ↓
Latent projection
        ↓
Initial recurrent hidden state
        ↓
Token embedding
        ↓
GRU decoder
        ↓
Linear vocabulary projection
        ↓
Token probabilities


Recommended baseline:

LATENT_DIM = 32

TOKEN_EMBED_DIM = 64

DECODER_HIDDEN_DIM = 128

NUM_GRU_LAYERS = 2


This is computationally manageable for the current molecular corpus.


==================================================
7. LATENT CONDITIONING
==================================================

The decoder must actually depend on the molecular latent representation.


One baseline strategy is:

z
↓
Linear projection
↓
initial GRU hidden state


For two GRU layers:

z
→
hidden states for decoder layers


This makes sequence generation conditional on the learned molecular
representation.


An optional later extension may concatenate a projected latent vector with each
token embedding.


==================================================
8. TEACHER-FORCED DECODER TRAINING
==================================================

During decoder training, use teacher forcing.


For target sequence:

<BOS> T1 T2 T3 ... TN <EOS>


decoder input:

<BOS> T1 T2 T3 ... TN


prediction target:

T1 T2 T3 ... TN <EOS>


The decoder learns:

P(
    token_t
    |
    previous tokens,
    z
)


==================================================
9. DECODER LOSS
==================================================

Use token-level categorical cross entropy.


The PAD token must be ignored in loss calculation.


Conceptually:

L_decoder
=
CrossEntropy(
    predicted_token_distribution,
    true_next_token
)


This is different from the Phase-10 structural reconstruction loss.


==================================================
10. ENCODER POLICY
==================================================

For the initial Phase-11 baseline, the Phase-10 encoder should preferably be:

FROZEN


during sequence-decoder training.


Therefore:

trained Phase-10 encoder
        ↓
fixed z = μ
        ↓
train generative decoder


This preserves the already validated baseline latent representation and allows
decoder performance to be evaluated independently.


Later experiments may fine-tune:

encoder + decoder jointly


but that should be treated as a separate experiment because joint fine-tuning
changes the previously learned latent representation.


==================================================
11. TRAINING LATENT REPRESENTATION
==================================================

Use deterministic Phase-10 embeddings:

z = μ


for decoder training.


This avoids introducing unnecessary latent sampling noise while establishing
the first sequence-generation baseline.


Therefore:

Phase-10 training molecule
        ↓
μ ∈ R^32
        ↓
SELFIES sequence


becomes a paired training sample.


==================================================
12. DECODER TRAINING PROCEDURE
==================================================

For each training molecule:

1. Retrieve drug_id.

2. Retrieve deterministic latent vector μ.

3. Retrieve standardized SMILES.

4. Convert SMILES to SELFIES.

5. Tokenize SELFIES.

6. Add BOS and EOS tokens.

7. Pad sequence.

8. Project latent vector into decoder hidden state.

9. Apply teacher forcing.

10. Predict next token.

11. Calculate cross-entropy loss.

12. Backpropagate through decoder.

13. Update decoder parameters.


The Phase-10 encoder remains frozen in the baseline decoder experiment.


==================================================
13. VALIDATION
==================================================

Validation should report at minimum:

validation token loss

token accuracy

exact sequence reconstruction rate

SELFIES decode success

RDKit parse success

canonical molecule reconstruction rate


The best decoder checkpoint should be selected using validation performance.


==================================================
14. EXACT MOLECULE RECONSTRUCTION
==================================================

Token-level accuracy alone is insufficient.


A decoded sequence may differ token-wise but still represent the same molecular
structure.


Therefore molecular reconstruction should also be evaluated after:

SELFIES → SMILES
↓
RDKit parse
↓
standardization/canonicalization


Then compare:

predicted canonical SMILES

against:

reference canonical standardized SMILES


This provides a chemically meaningful reconstruction metric.


==================================================
15. GENERATION MODES
==================================================

Phase 11 should support at least two modes.


MODE A — LATENT RECONSTRUCTION

Known molecule
↓
trained encoder
↓
μ
↓
decoder
↓
reconstructed molecule


This tests whether the latent representation can be decoded.


MODE B — LATENT PERTURBATION GENERATION

Known latent vector:

z


Create:

z'
=
z
+
δ


where:

δ

is a small controlled perturbation.


Then:

z'
↓
decoder
↓
candidate molecule


This allows local exploration around known molecular regions.


==================================================
16. RANDOM PRIOR SAMPLING
==================================================

The VAE formulation also permits sampling:

z ~ N(0,I)


and decoding z.


However, random prior sampling should be treated as an exploratory experiment.


Because Phase 10 used a small KL weight:

β = 0.001


the aggregate learned latent distribution may not perfectly match the standard
normal prior.


Therefore candidate validity from random prior sampling must be measured
rather than assumed.


==================================================
17. GENERATION STRATEGY
==================================================

The decoder should support configurable token-selection strategies.


Baseline options:

greedy decoding

temperature sampling

top-k sampling


Recommended initial validation:

greedy decoding


Recommended candidate-generation experiment:

temperature sampling


Example baseline:

TEMPERATURE = 1.0


Optional:

TOP_K = 10


These are experimental parameters and should be recorded.


==================================================
18. GENERATION TERMINATION
==================================================

Generation stops when:

<EOS>

is produced


or when:

MAX_SEQUENCE_LENGTH

is reached.


Generated PAD tokens should not be interpreted as molecular tokens.


==================================================
19. GENERATED MOLECULE VALIDATION PIPELINE
==================================================

Every generated molecular candidate must pass the following sequence:


Generated token sequence
        ↓
SELFIES syntax / decoding check
        ↓
Convert SELFIES to SMILES
        ↓
RDKit molecular parsing
        ↓
RDKit sanitization
        ↓
Valence validation
        ↓
Standardization
        ↓
Canonical SMILES generation
        ↓
Molecular feasibility checks
        ↓
Duplicate removal
        ↓
Novelty assessment
        ↓
Accepted candidate


==================================================
20. SYNTAX VALIDATION
==================================================

Check whether:

generated token sequence

can be converted into a valid SELFIES molecular representation.


If decoding fails:

reject candidate


Record the reason:

SELFIES_DECODE_FAILURE


==================================================
21. CHEMICAL PARSING
==================================================

Convert generated SELFIES to:

SMILES


Then construct:

RDKit Mol


If parsing fails:

reject candidate


Record:

RDKIT_PARSE_FAILURE


==================================================
22. SANITIZATION
==================================================

Each parsed molecule must pass RDKit sanitization.


This checks important chemical consistency constraints.


If sanitization fails:

reject candidate


Record:

SANITIZATION_FAILURE


==================================================
23. VALENCE VALIDATION
==================================================

Generated

PHASE 12 — BASELINE SYSTEM CONSOLIDATION, PREDICTOR TRAINING, AND REFERENCE-STATE ESTABLISHMENT


OBJECTIVE

Phase 12 establishes the complete baseline reference state of the molecular
discovery system before any closed-loop adaptation, continual learning, Fisher
information calculation, or Elastic Weight Consolidation is performed.


Earlier phases have already established:

Phase 10:
Trained baseline geometry-aware variational encoder

Phase 10:
Baseline continuous molecular latent representation

Phase 11:
Trained latent-conditioned molecular generative decoder


Therefore Phase 12 should NOT retrain these components from scratch.


Instead, Phase 12 should:

1. Load the best trained baseline encoder.

2. Load the best trained generative decoder.

3. Train and validate the baseline biological-relevance predictor.

4. Establish the fixed baseline latent representation Z0.

5. Consolidate encoder, decoder, predictor, preprocessing metadata, and baseline
   statistics.

6. Freeze the complete baseline parameter state.

7. Save the reference parameter state against which later adaptation and
   parameter drift will be measured.


==================================================
BASELINE SYSTEM COMPONENTS
==================================================

The baseline molecular discovery system contains three principal learnable
components:


ENCODER

Parameters:

θE*


Function:

Molecular Graph
↓
Geometry-Aware Equivariant Encoder
↓
Latent Molecular Representation


The trained encoder comes from Phase 10.


--------------------------------------------------

GENERATIVE DECODER

Parameters:

θD*


Function:

Latent Molecular Representation
↓
Latent-Conditioned SELFIES Decoder
↓
Molecular Candidate Representation


The trained generative decoder comes from Phase 11.


--------------------------------------------------

PREDICTOR

Parameters:

θP*


Function:

Latent Molecular Representation
and/or molecular representation
↓
Biological-Relevance Predictor
↓
Baseline Predictive Score


The predictor should be trained in Phase 12 using only biological information
that is legitimately available from the DrugBank-derived baseline corpus.


==================================================
IMPORTANT TERMINOLOGY
==================================================

The predictor should NOT be called a:

binding-affinity predictor


unless quantitative experimental affinity data such as:

Ki
Kd
IC50
EC50

are actually available and used as labels.


The DrugBank target associations extracted earlier provide:

drug-target associations

known-action information

actions

organism information

protein/polypeptide information


Therefore the safest baseline terminology is:

biological-relevance predictor

or:

target-association predictor


depending on the exact prediction objective selected.


==================================================
BASELINE LATENT MANIFOLD
==================================================

Phase 10 established deterministic molecular latent vectors:

z = μ


for the baseline molecular corpus.


These vectors define the baseline latent representation:

Z0


Conceptually:

DrugBank-Derived Molecular Graphs
        ↓
Trained Baseline Encoder θE*
        ↓
μ
        ↓
Z0


Because the Phase-10 encoder was frozen during Phase 11 decoder training:

Z0

remains the reference latent molecular representation unless the encoder is
subsequently fine-tuned.


==================================================
IMPORTANT DISTINCTION
==================================================

The following statements should remain separate:


XML

=

baseline chemical and biological knowledge source


Graph corpus

=

computational molecular representation


Z0

=

learned baseline latent molecular representation


Θ*

=

complete frozen baseline model parameter state


==================================================
PRIMARY INPUTS
==================================================

Phase 8 provides:

Training corpus   = 613 graphs

Validation corpus = 76 graphs

Test corpus       = 78 graphs

Fisher reference  = 128 training-derived graphs


Phase 10 provides:

phase10_best_encoder.pt

phase10_train_latent.csv

phase10_validation_latent.csv

phase10_test_latent.csv


Phase 11 provides:

phase11_best_generative_decoder.pt


Phase 6 provides:

D_bio_association


which contains the DrugBank-derived biological association information.


==================================================
1. BASELINE ENCODER STATE
==================================================

Load the best trained encoder checkpoint from Phase 10.


The baseline encoder parameters are denoted:

θE*


These parameters must NOT be modified during reference-state establishment.


The encoder should be placed in evaluation mode when baseline latent vectors are
recomputed or verified.


==================================================
2. BASELINE DECODER STATE
==================================================

Load the best trained molecular generative decoder from Phase 11.


The baseline decoder parameters are denoted:

θD*


These parameters represent the baseline latent-to-molecule generation state.


They must be frozen before later closed-loop adaptation begins.


==================================================
3. BASELINE PREDICTOR
==================================================

Phase 12 should introduce the predictor required by the later candidate
evaluation and closed-loop prioritization stages.


Recommended baseline objective:

predict DrugBank-grounded biological relevance from the molecular latent
representation.


A practical baseline predictor may operate on:

z = μ ∈ R^32


Conceptually:

z
↓
Fully Connected Layer
↓
Nonlinearity
↓
Output Layer
↓
Biological-Relevance Prediction


==================================================
4. PREDICTOR TARGET DESIGN
==================================================

The exact predictor label must be defined carefully.


One practical baseline is:

HAS BIOLOGICAL ASSOCIATION


Binary target:

1
=
molecule has one or more DrugBank target associations


0
=
molecule has no DrugBank target association


However, because almost all current graph molecules have biological
associations, this target may be highly imbalanced and may provide limited
learning value.


A stronger alternative is a multi-label target representation based on:

selected DrugBank targets

target families

action categories

or biological association classes


The final target must be selected based on:

class support

sample count

data imbalance

biological interpretability


==================================================
5. RECOMMENDED PREDICTOR STRATEGY
==================================================

For the current baseline corpus, a more informative predictor is recommended:


MULTI-LABEL TARGET-ASSOCIATION PREDICTOR


For each molecule:

z ∈ R^32


predict:

y ∈ {0,1}^K


where:

K

is the number of selected sufficiently supported biological target classes.


To avoid extremely sparse outputs, only targets meeting a predefined minimum
training-support threshold should be included.


For example:

MIN_TARGET_SUPPORT = 5


The exact threshold must be reported.


==================================================
6. TRAINING-ONLY LABEL CONSTRUCTION
==================================================

The predictor label space must be defined using:

TRAINING DATA ONLY


This prevents information leakage from validation and test molecules.


Therefore:

training biological associations
↓
target-frequency calculation
↓
supported target selection
↓
fixed target vocabulary


Validation and test molecules are then projected into the same target space.


==================================================
7. PREDICTOR ARCHITECTURE
==================================================

A lightweight baseline is appropriate.


Recommended architecture:

32
↓
64
↓
32
↓
K


with:

SiLU or ReLU

dropout if required

sigmoid output during inference


The predictor output layer should have:

K dimensions


for multi-label target prediction.


==================================================
8. PREDICTOR LOSS
==================================================

For multi-label prediction use:

Binary Cross Entropy with Logits


Conceptually:

L_predictor
=
BCEWithLogitsLoss(
    predicted logits,
    true multi-label target vector
)


If class imbalance is substantial, positive-class weighting may be estimated
using:

TRAINING DATA ONLY.


==================================================
9. PREDICTOR DATA POLICY
==================================================

Only training molecules may update:

θP


Validation molecules may be used for:

early stopping

hyperparameter selection

checkpoint selection


Test molecules must remain excluded until the best predictor checkpoint has
been selected.


==================================================
10. ENCODER POLICY DURING PREDICTOR TRAINING
==================================================

The baseline encoder should remain:

FROZEN


during predictor training.


Therefore:

molecular graph
↓
fixed trained encoder
↓
z = μ
↓
predictor


or equivalently use the already saved deterministic Phase-10 latent vectors.


This keeps:

θE*

unchanged while learning:

θP*


==================================================
11. PREDICTOR VALIDATION METRICS
==================================================

Because the task is multi-label, report metrics such as:

micro F1

macro F1

micro precision

micro recall

average precision

ROC-AUC where mathematically defined


Do not rely on simple classification accuracy alone.


==================================================
12. BASELINE PREDICTOR CHECKPOINT
==================================================

After validation-based model selection, save:

θP*


as the baseline predictor state.


Recommended file:

phase12_best_baseline_predictor.pt


==================================================
13. COMPLETE BASELINE PARAMETER STATE
==================================================

After all baseline components are available, define:

Θ*

as:

Θ*
=
{
    θE*,
    θD*,
    θP*
}


where:

θE*
=
trained baseline encoder parameters


θD*
=
trained baseline molecular decoder parameters


θP*
=
trained baseline predictor parameters


==================================================
14. BASELINE LATENT REFERENCE
==================================================

The baseline latent representation is:

Z0


with:

Z0
=
{
    μ(G1),
    μ(G2),
    ...
}


for the baseline molecular corpus.


The deterministic representation:

z = μ


should be used for reference-state comparisons.


==================================================
15. BASELINE SYSTEM SNAPSHOT
==================================================

The baseline system snapshot should include more than neural-network weights.


It should preserve:

encoder parameters

decoder parameters

predictor parameters

latent dimension

hidden dimensions

model architectures

SELFIES vocabulary

feature normalization

target label vocabulary

predictor label schema

Phase-8 split assignments

baseline latent vectors

DrugBank dataset version

random seed

training configuration

software/library versions where practical


This allows the baseline state to be reconstructed exactly.


==================================================
16. PARAMETER-DRIFT REFERENCE
==================================================

Later closed-loop adaptation will produce updated model parameters:

Θ(t)


Parameter drift should be measured relative to:

Θ*


For a parameter tensor θ:

Δθ
=
θ(t)
-
θ*


Possible drift measurements include:

L2 norm

relative L2 norm

cosine change

layer-wise parameter displacement


Phase 12 should establish the reference state only.


It should NOT yet perform adaptation.


==================================================
17. LATENT-DRIFT REFERENCE
==================================================

Later adaptation may also change the encoder representation.


Therefore retain the fixed baseline latent vectors:

Z0


For a reference molecule G:

z0(G)

=
baseline latent vector


Later:

zt(G)

=
adapted latent vector


Latent drift may then be measured as:

||zt(G) - z0(G)||


This is different from parameter drift and should be tracked separately.


==================================================
18. FISHER REFERENCE POLICY
==================================================

Phase 8 created the fixed Fisher-reference subset.


During Phase 12:

do NOT yet perform EWC.


Fisher information may be calculated in the subsequent continual-learning
reference phase using the finalized baseline model.


The Fisher subset must remain unchanged.


==================================================
19. MODEL HASH / INTEGRITY CHECK
==================================================

For reproducibility, Phase 12 should calculate and store a deterministic
checksum or hash for the baseline model checkpoints.


At minimum record hashes for:

baseline encoder checkpoint

baseline decoder checkpoint

baseline predictor checkpoint


This helps verify later that:

Θ*

has not been accidentally overwritten.


==================================================
20. BASELINE SYSTEM VALIDATION
==================================================

Before freezing Θ*, verify:

encoder checkpoint reloads successfully

decoder checkpoint reloads successfully

predictor checkpoint reloads successfully

latent dimension = 32

baseline embeddings are finite

decoder can generate from baseline embeddings

predictor produces finite outputs

training/validation/test assignments remain unchanged

Fisher subset remains unchanged


==================================================
21. WHAT PHASE 12 SHOULD PERFORM
==================================================

Phase 12 should perform:

load trained Phase-10 encoder

load trained Phase-11 decoder

construct baseline predictor labels

Phase 12 should NOT perform:

Those belong to later phases.
